purpose: Source-only manual coverage checklist frozen before reading the generated graph. Diagnostic review, not an independent benchmark or question-derived gold set.

source.title: 200+ of the best deals from Amazon's Cyber Monday sale

review_rules: The checklist was derived only from the first complete article record, without questions, answers, evidence labels or generated graph output.
Count distinct supported meanings, not edge quantity. Several checklist rows may be correctly represented by one qualified fact or structured offer.

Required retrieval means a participant and predicate/value/condition are reachable through graph reads; a value found only by reading the original source is source-access coverage, not graph-fact coverage.
Preserve reported, subjective, comparative and uncertain claims as such. Source support is not independent verification.

The original record contains many category headings but omits individual product lists. Do not invent the advertised 200-plus individual deals or infer that every heading names a currently available concrete offer.
Do not infer exact product models, sale prices, currencies, predecessor identifiers, numerical review counts or offer validity boundaries absent from the source.
Publication metadata and the in-body update label are distinct values; neither should silently overwrite the other.
Navigation, editorial wording and publication metadata are audited separately from substantive domain assertions; they must not inflate domain-fact completeness.

editorial_and_publication_meanings.meaning: Mashable publishes this named Amazon Cyber Monday deal roundup at the recorded URL, with the supplied publication timestamp and a separate in-body update label.
The body says the post was updated with the latest Amazon Cyber Monday deals; this is a reported update, not a guarantee of live availability after publication.
Mashable describes a running curated list, spotlighting favorites, noting sellouts and intending repeated updates while the sale continues.
Mashable refers to another larger Cyber Monday list spanning more retailers; no link target or contents are supplied here.
Sparkle marker means a newly added deal.
Fire marker means an all-time-low price.
Envelope marker means an Amazon invite-only deal for Prime members; invite requirement and Prime eligibility are both material.
Strikethrough means sold out OR expired at writing time. The legend alone does not identify which condition applied to an individual offer.

The article recommends Echo Show as a useful room addition, with hands-free Alexa tasks and audiovisual uses as reasons. Subjective game-changing/easier-life wording is editorial, not measured effectiveness.
The article now favors the tenth-generation 64GB iPad Amazon offer, in the context of ninth-generation stock fluctuations.
The article recommends the featured 65-inch Fire TV, citing display, brightness, artwork/photo display and Alexa capabilities.
The article calls the older Surface Go 2 its favorite budget laptop and praises the Go 3 offer; those are reviewer preferences.
The Go 3's appearance is compared to MacBook Air; resemblance must not merge product identities or invent shared technical specifications.
Bose is described as premium and reputable, QC45 ANC as top-of-the-line and its comfort as all-day. Preserve attribution/subjectivity if stored.
Echo devices are organized under Amazon device/service deals; Apple Watches and MacBooks are organized under Apple deals. These are article section placements, not taxonomic is-a facts.
Mashable advertises a daily Deals newsletter; the sign-up wording says subscribers agree to its Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Loading/thank-you UI text is not evidence that this reader subscribed.

section_coverage.meaning: Named article sections/subsections can provide source navigation or topic coverage. They do not establish unlisted concrete offers, prices or product availability.

negative_checks: No fabricated individual deals for category headings whose lists are absent.
No exact Echo Show price/model beyond the <40 bound and stated 5.5-inch feature.
No exact 65-inch Fire TV price/model beyond the reported historical-low claim and features.
No guaranteed ninth-generation iPad availability or a claim that its possible price is always current.
No computed Go 3 original price, AirPods Max price or MGM+ monthly price represented as source-explicit facts.
No promotion code moved from the Quest credit eligibility to the base device sale price.
No offer-specific qualification detached from its named offer, beneficiary or subscription.
No inferred author identity, repaired timestamp, invented current validity or unstated hardware generation.
No generic RELATED_TO edges substituted for the concrete named price, eligibility, feature, comparison or publication predicate.
No independent evidential count added for article headings, repeated TOC text or a graph restatement of the same source.
